findings.title: Exercise legacy-only status detail round trips
findings.why_it_matters: Existing callers can attach details generated by the older protobuf generator and type-assert decoded details back to that concrete message. This changed assertion requires every expected detail to implement ProtoReflect, so the test cannot exercise that supported MessageV1-only case; all fixtures implement both APIs. The new Details implementation returns the protobuf reflection wrapper for legacy messages rather than the original concrete type, and these tests still pass. A legacy-only fixture with a concrete-type assertion would expose that compatibility regression.
findings.suggested_fix: Extend TestStatus_ErrorDetails with a registered legacy-only generated message implementing Reset, String, and ProtoMessage without ProtoReflect. Assert the returned details count and original concrete type, then compare field values; use protoadapt.MessageV2Of for semantic protobuf comparisons instead of directly asserting all inputs implement protoreflect.ProtoMessage. Preserve the concrete return type in Details with protoadapt.MessageV1Of(detail).
evidence: status/status_test.go:318-347 -- Every nonempty case uses modern ResourceInfo, DebugInfo, or RetryInfo; no MessageV1-only fixture is supplied.

testing_gaps: encoding/proto/proto.go:27 changes the accepted message interface, but encoding/proto/proto_test.go exercises only test/codec_perf.Buffer, which has ProtoReflect. Add a legacy-only generated/custom message case through encoding.GetCodec("proto") that checks both Marshal wire bytes and Unmarshal into a fresh destination; the current interface assertions reject that existing caller class.

internal/binarylog/method_logger.go:242 and :282 now recognize only modern protobuf messages. TestLog supplies modern binlogpb.Message or []byte, so it misses a legacy-only RPC message being logged with empty Data and zero Length. Add client and server log cases using a legacy-only message and independently expected protobuf bytes.

balancer/rls/config.go:310 now clamps time.Duration overflow while reporting no error for protobuf-valid values. Existing TestParseConfigErrors duration cases use 315576000001s, which protojson rejects before convertDuration. Extend the existing parser table with 9223372036.854775808s (and the corresponding negative boundary) for lookupServiceTimeout, maxAge, and staleAge, asserting the prior overflow error rather than saturation; include exact representable boundaries as successful cases.

xds/internal/xdsclient/transport/loadreport.go:174-177 replaces interval validation and conversion, but loadreport tests only send a valid 50ms interval. Add malformed/nil interval cases asserting the actual validation error is retained (the current error formats the earlier nil Recv error), and a protobuf-valid interval above time.Duration's range asserting rejection rather than an effectively permanent reporting delay.
